newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels step up attacks on key pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels step up attacks on key pipeline.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels dynamited Colombia's Cano Limon pipeline for the second time this week Tuesday and spokesmen for the state oil company, Ecopetrol, said pumping along the line had been suspended since Sunday.
The pipeline carries about 200,000 barrels of crude oil per day from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean port of Covenas.
Ecopetrol spokesmen said the latest attack on the line occurred early Tuesday, just as pumping operations were set to resume following another attack Sunday.
"We never managed to get it started again," one of the spokesmen said, adding that up to 13,000 barrels of crude have been spilled in three attacks on the structure since June 11.

In all, the pipeline has been blown up 34 times so far this year. All of the attacks are thought to be the work of National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels, who dynamited the pipeline 47 times last year and spilled more than 105,000 barrels of crude.
The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, was founded by radical Roman Cathlic priests in 1966 and specializes in kidnapping as well as attacks on oil and coal facilities.

Chief Ecopetrol spokesman William Giraldo said the latest rupture in the pipeline was in an accessible area near the Cao Limon oil fields and added that repair work should be completed sometime Wednesday when pumping operations would hopefully resume.
